_readme: Resolutions for the duplicate sections in abroad3.docx, so that whoever
imports it does not have to re-derive these decisions or guess.
abroad3.docx is a database kept in Word: 18 phases, 54 country guides and
121 course records. Parts of it were regenerated rather than edited, so a
few sections exist twice with DIFFERENT WORDING. Textual dedupe cannot
resolve those - the two copies share very few lines - and picking the
longer one is not always right either. The rule used here is:
RULE: keep the copy that satisfies the document's own A-Q section
schema. Where both are complete, keep the one with more numbered
questions. Never merge two copies: they are independently written and
interleaving them produces claims neither source makes.
Line numbers refer to a `pdftotext`-free plain-text extraction of the
converted_txt/abroad__abroad3.docx.txt). They WILL drift if the .docx is
re-exported - match on the heading text, and treat the line numbers as a

duplicates.heading: 13.5 CANADA - COUNTRY-WISE EDUCATION GUIDE
why: The kept copy completes the document's own A-Q schema; the dropped one
stops at P. It also carries 6 more questions, and names Canada's PAL
(Provincial Attestation Letter) which the dropped copy omits entirely.
Only 17 lines are shared between them, so this is a rewrite, not a
copy-paste: do not attempt a textual merge.

duplicates.heading: 1. Why study in Greece?
why: Both copies complete the A-Q schema, so the tie-break applies: the kept
copy answers 6 more questions. 192 lines are shared and ~300 differ on
each side - again a rewrite, not a copy-paste.

finding: NOT a duplicate, despite both being headed 'PHASE 11 - SUBJECTS,
STREAMS & COURSE OPTIONS ABROAD' and both opening at '11.1'.
The first is general guidance on how to choose a course (2,787 words);
the second is the stream-by-stream catalogue, opening at '11.1 SCIENCE
STREAM' (3,823 words). They share 221 lines out of ~950.
KEEP BOTH. Deleting either loses real content. Treat the first as the
phase introduction and the second as its body, and renumber the second
block's subsections when importing so two sections do not both claim
Present, not missing. Its heading carries a leading emoji
('🌍 PHASE 14 - UNIVERSITY & COLLEGE GUIDE'), so a pattern anchored on
'^PHASE' skips it and the phase list looks like it jumps 13 -> 15.
Anchor on the phase number, not the line start.

detail: The country guides name live instruments - Canada PGWP/PAL/TAL,
Australia's Genuine Student test, the UK Graduate visa, US OPT/CPT -
with no date stamp anywhere in the document, and no 'not immigration
advice' line. One claim has a hard expiry: the UK Graduate visa text
states 2 years for applications 'on or before 31 December 2026'.
This is a publishing decision, not a parsing one. Do not publish the

open_for_a_human.what: Generation chat left in the body
detail: Conversational residue survives in the document text (for example
'YESSS - now I understand the level of detail you want.'). The guide
importer's noise filter does not cover these; they need removing at
the source or an added rule before any of this ships.
